Adding a 3x3 conv to a skip-dominated cell gives about +45 on C10 and C100, versus a few points elsewhere.
A cell with no learnable convs benefits most from its first 3x3 conv.
The conv edit gives a +33 to +35 jump on C10 and C100 in a skip-heavy parent, versus about 0 to 3 in mixed parents.
The edit gives +33 on C10 in a parent with no convs, but under 1 point in mixed parents that already have convs.
Replacing a skip edge with none helps (+42 in the all-skip parent, small positives in the mixed one), whereas removing conv edges hurts.
Removing a skip edge improves accuracy (+28 in the all-skip parent, +1.5 to +3.5 in the mixed one), while removing a conv edge hurts.
Replacing a skip edge with none is positive or neutral (+27.8 in the all-skip parent), unlike removing a conv edge, which loses accuracy.
Dropping a skip edge helps the skip-dominated parent (+27 on C10), unlike dropping other ops.
Replacing a pooling edge with a conv gives about +35 on C10 in the all-pool parent, versus near zero when the edge already holds a conv.

In particular, the 1x1-conv parent often has larger ImageNet16-120 gains than the mixed parents that satisfy the condition.
